label: late original-phase j/v/1/n/a/y/k/c in sequences starting with u/b/p/g/d/w
explanation: Fires almost only during the original (input) phase (99.8% of mass), at positions t>=3 (none at t=0,1, rare at t=2), when the input is one of a preferred set of tokens (j, v, 1 strongest, then n, a, y, k, c), mostly the first occurrence of that token. It depends on sequence context: it is much more likely when the first original token is u or b (and less so p, g, d, w). Near-silent at the delimiter and during copy, and for inputs such as m, x, e, h. The highest activations come from inputs j/v/1 in sequences starting with u or b. The predicate covers about 68% of activation mass, but precision is only about 0.4. Inside the predicate, firing depends on the earlier tokens in a way a simple rule does not capture, so the context dependence looks distributed.
